Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.

dimensions.assessment: Applies to any person who registers an account or accesses a covered platform, and all commercial covered platform providers operating in the United States.
dimensions.evidence: A covered platform provider shall-- (1) each time a user accesses the covered platform of the provider while physically located in the United States, clearly and conspicuously display a mental health warning label

dimensions.assessment: Platform providers must display warning labels and comply with FTC regulations, while users encounter mandatory warning prompts upon access and continuously per hour of use.
dimensions.evidence: cause the covered label to disappear only if the user-- (A) exits the covered platform; or (B) acknowledges the potential for harm and chooses to proceed

dimensions.assessment: The source does not specify exact federal appropriations but creates enforcement mechanisms involving civil penalties and potential state-level actions.
dimensions.evidence: liable for a civil penalty equal to the amount calculated by multiplying-- (A) the greater of-- (i) the number of days during which the covered platform provider was not in compliance

dimensions.assessment: Requires new regulations promulgated by the FTC and the Secretary of Health and Human Services, enforced under FTC Act rules and state attorney general authority.
dimensions.evidence: the Commission, with the concurrence of the Secretary acting through the Surgeon General, shall promulgate regulations containing appropriate requirements for a covered label.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory requirement taking effect one year after enactment, with ongoing 5-year reviews of regulations by federal agencies.
dimensions.evidence: This Act shall take effect on the date that is 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific figures on federal administrative costs or appropriated funding amounts.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates mental health warning labels on all covered social media and anonymous content sharing platforms used in the United States. It involves broad regulatory implementation by the FTC and HHS, potential civil penalties for violations, and multi-year reviews, affecting online service providers and all platform users nationwide.
